item.title: SCP-3653:
item.content:encoded: Isn't there another SCP that adds days to the calendar or year, and people know about it during that time, leading to reckless behavior since there cannot be any consequences since it will be reverted at the end of the extra time and no one will remember?

item.content:encoded: Well, I never said it didn't work. You'll just have to ponder why there might be standing orders from the Administrator to keep thirteen specific individuals alive for an extremely long time.

item.title: SCP-509:
item.content:encoded:
I'm in agreement, if we can put in a live pig, why not a dead human (I'm sure the foundation, um, has a few of those to spare?)
I think that's a sign that this is a good SCP: I'm not irritated by the omissions, but I want to know more. One gets the sense of being this close to being able to explain everything, and it's tantalizing.

item.title: SCP-5921: -1 :{
item.content:encoded:
This doesn't work for me -
For 1: There isn't a story, it's just a thing that kills you, and nothing more. It just seems designed to be a spooky satan armour.

For 2: It is riddled with spelling mistakes, for instance:

Description: is…

Shouldn't it say SCP-XXXX is? This is only one example of this.

For these reasons, I'll have to downvote this. I would try and go through the correct procedures for getting an article e.g

Ideas critique ---> Draft Critique ----> Posting.

-1.

item.title: SCP-085: My feelings exactly
item.content:encoded:
Not every SCP is designed to inspire horror or lust; for the Foundation to notice an anomaly, it only needs to be inconsistent with "ordinary" reality and scientific laws. A sentient drawing enhanced by alien technology? Study it in captivity; Cassie doesn't have to be evil, spooky, or sexy to be interesting to scientists.

*grabs a sketch pad and offers Cassie a drawing of an ordinary teddy bear — friendly, innocent-faced, and very huggable*
